properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md-5 crate appears transitively in Cargo.lock (RustCrypto MD5); no direct call site anywhere in workspace code (verified by grep). MD5 is collision-broken (CWE-328 risk if ever used) — it ships only as an unused transitive dependency; candidate for dependency pruning.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1 crate appears transitively in Cargo.lock (RustCrypto SHA-1, e.g. via libp2p multihash legacy-hash support); no direct call site in workspace code. SHA-1 is collision-broken — ships only as an unused transitive dependency; candidate for pruning.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA on secp256k1 is one of Substrate's three account/consensus signature schemes: recoverable ECDSA signing via the secp256k1 crate global context (primitives/core/src/ecdsa.rs:754 SECP256K1.sign_ecdsa_recoverable), recovery host functions exposed to runtimes (primitives/io/src/lib.rs:1112-1116 via libsecp256k1; sp_io::crypto::secp256k1_ecdsa_recover_compressed), consumed by pallet-contracts (frame/contracts/src/exec.rs:1449, recovering Ethereum-style addresses), BEEFY mandatory justification

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile face of the ECDSA-secp256k1 scheme already inventoried at code level (ALG-673c8f24: sp-core ecdsa sign_ecdsa_recoverable, sp_io recovery host functions, pallet-contracts, BEEFY). The Cargo.lock entries are the secp256k1/k256 RustCrypto crates providing that ECDSA. Shor-vulnerable; migrate to ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Cargo.toml:336 line is the chacha20poly1305 profile entry — the Poly1305 MAC exists here only as the authentication half of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD that snow (libp2p Noise transport) uses for sc-network session encryption. Same logical asset as the ChaCha20-Poly1305 object ALG-3d4cff53. Poly1305 is PQ-secure as a MAC; the channel's PQ risk is the X25519 Noise handshake.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is Substrate's second account/consensus signature scheme, implemented in sp-core via ed25519-zebra 3.1.0 (ed25519.rs:42 use ed25519_zebra::{SigningKey, VerificationKey}; verify at :426). Live uses: libp2p node identity keys (generate_node_key.rs:51 ed25519::Keypair::generate, config.rs:343), GRANDPA/session keys where configured, CLI scheme selection, test keyring. Shor breaks EdDSA discrete log → forgeable signatures; migrate to ML-DSA-65. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile face of X25519 already inventoried at code level (ALG-1138d04b: statement-store ECIES ephemeral Diffie-Hellman plus libp2p-noise/snow handshake key agreement). Harvest-now-decrypt-later; migrate to ML-KEM-768 hybrid.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile face of the curve25519-dalek group library backing X25519 ECDH (statement-store ECIES, ALG-1138d04b) and the Edwards-point conversions in ecies.rs:96-97. Same logical asset family as the X25519 object. Shor-vulnerable group arithmetic.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: p256 (NIST P-256 ECDSA, RustCrypto) appears transitively in Cargo.lock; no direct call site in workspace code — shipped capability only, not exercised by Substrate's own schemes. If ever used, P-256 ECDSA is Shor-vulnerable; PQ replacement would be ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (SHA-3 family) is a live hashing layer: BEEFY keystore prehashes signed messages with keccak_256 before ECDSA signing (keystore.rs:33 BeefySignatureHasher = Keccak256, keystore.rs:77), pallet-contracts meters storage via hash_keccak_256 (wasm/runtime.rs:339-340), and pallet-identity accepts Keccak256 judgements. Keccak/SHA-3 is post-quantum secure — no Shor exposure; recorded as the shipped hashing layer. PQ-secure, no migration needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE2b/BLAKE3 are Substrate's primary hash functions: BlakeTwo256 is the default state-trie and block hash (sp-core-hashing blake2_256/blake2_128, used everywhere from runtime API dispatch IDs (decl_runtime_apis.rs:499) to key-derivation junctions), Blake2b-512 in frame/glutton, and blake2b256 multihash CIDs in the bitswap content-addressing client. BLAKE2/3 are PQ-secure hashes — no Shor exposure; recorded as the shipped hashing layer.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-GCM is the AEAD half of the statement-store ECIES scheme (primitives/statement-store/src/ecies.rs): Aes256Gcm::new at L51/L58 seals/opens statement payloads, nonce freshly generated from OsRng at L82. AES-GCM itself is symmetric and post-quantum secure; the PQ risk in the chain is the X25519 ECDH feeding the HKDF key. Recorded as the shipped AEAD plus its aes-gcm crate dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 (hkdf 0.12) derives the AES-256-GCM key from the X25519 Diffie-Hellman shared secret in statement-store ECIES (ecies.rs:63-69: Hkdf::<sha2::Sha256>::new(None, shared_secret) then expand to a 32-byte key). HKDF is PQ-secure as a KDF; its secrecy inherits the X25519 agreement, which is the quantum-vulnerable link.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC appears in Cargo.lock as the hmac crate, feeding the two KDFs already inventoried: substrate-bip39's PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 mnemonic KDF (reported as finding at primitives/core/src/crypto.rs:881-883) and HKDF-SHA256 in statement-store ECIES (ecies.rs:64). HMAC is PQ-secure as a MAC/KDF building block.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2 crate in Cargo.lock is the implementation behind substrate-bip39's seed_from_entropy (live call site reported separately: primitives/core/src/crypto.rs:881-883, 2048 iterations, BIP39). The iteration count is below modern OWASP guidance (CWE-916) though the KDF itself is PQ-safe.
